title: The Modern Attack Surface
summary: A tour of how attack surfaces have sprawled across cloud, APIs, and supply chains.
body:
Modern applications rarely fail because of one dramatic flaw. More often it's a chain: an input nobody thought to bound, a calculation nobody re-checked downstream, and a trust decision made one layer too early. Attackers don't need a zero-day when a billing API and an entitlement check quietly disagree about what actually happened.

We'll be writing more about business logic flaws like these in the coming weeks — the kind that pass every unit test because each component, in isolation, does exactly what it was told to do.

title: Securing CI/CD Pipelines
summary: Practical hardening steps for build and deploy pipelines.
body: Pipeline security is mostly about reducing the blast radius of a single compromised step: least-privilege deploy credentials, signed artifacts, and reproducible builds. We'll publish a deep technical breakdown of a real pipeline compromise in our Premium research tier soon.

title: AWS IAM Misconfigurations
summary: Common IAM policy mistakes that quietly grant far more access than intended.
body: Over-permissive IAM policies rarely look dangerous on their own — it's the combination of a wildcard resource here and an inherited trust relationship there that adds up to full account takeover. This report walks through three real-world misconfiguration patterns and how to detect them with policy simulation.

title: OAuth 2.0 and OIDC in Practice
summary: A practitioner's guide to implementing OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect correctly.
body: Most OAuth implementation bugs live in the gap between the spec and the glue code: redirect URI validation, state parameter handling, and token audience checks. This report includes a checklist we use in client security reviews.

title: ISO 27001: From Controls to Evidence
summary: Turning ISO/IEC 27001 controls into audit-ready evidence without the busywork.
body: Control statements are easy to write and hard to operationalize. This report covers how to map Annex A controls to concrete, collectible evidence your auditor will actually accept the first time.

title: Advanced Web Application Testing
summary: Beyond the OWASP Top 10: testing techniques for modern web application logic.
body: Automated scanners find the vulnerabilities that look like vulnerabilities. The interesting bugs live in workflows that span multiple requests: a quote generated in one call and silently trusted in the next, with no re-verification in between. We cover a methodology for mapping these multi-step flows before you start poking at them.

title: Inside a Modern Ransomware Campaign
summary: A technical walkthrough of a 2026 ransomware affiliate operation, from initial access to extortion.
body: This campaign began, like most do, with a boring foothold: a reused credential on an exposed management interface. The interesting part is what happened after access — how the operators moved from a single host to domain-wide encryption in under six hours.

title: Business Logic Vulnerabilities in E-commerce
summary: How checkout flows quietly become the most exploitable part of an application.
body: Checkout is where price, quantity, inventory, and payment status all have to agree with each other, across several requests, without a human in the loop. When any one of those values is trusted a little too early — especially one derived from arithmetic that was written for a different era of hardware — the whole chain can be walked backwards by an attacker who's willing to be patient with edge cases. Fixed-width accumulators, in particular, have a long and embarrassing history of disagreeing with reality once a quantity field gets large enough.

title: The Zero Trust Architecture Playbook
summary: A practical rollout plan for zero trust across hybrid cloud environments.
body: Zero trust fails in practice when 'never trust, always verify' quietly becomes 'verify once, trust forever' at some internal service boundary. This report covers where that erosion tends to happen first.

title: Lina's Private Security Research
summary: Unreleased, invitation-only research. Pricing reflects its exclusivity — this is not meant to be purchased casually.
body:
You've reached Lina's private research vault. This content isn't priced for a casual reader, and that's deliberate — it exists to be shared only with a small number of serious collaborators.

Congratulations on unlocking it anyway.
